verdict.rationale: GitLab documents its own SAST feature, which scans project source code automatically on each commit and shows findings in merge requests and the code view. However, the evidence never names the vulnerability classes it detects, such as injection or XSS, or describes its rule coverage. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of detected vulnerability classes (injection, XSS), rule or language coverage details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of detection quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run static analysis that finds vulnerability classes like injection and XSS in my source code

citations.quote: Application security testing scans your project’s source code, dependencies, libraries, and container images.
Enable SAST in your project by using either the UI or editing your project’s GitLab CI/CD configuration file.
SAST scans happen automatically with each commit, giving you immediate feedback without disrupting your workflow.
Merge request changes view: Shows inline annotations for changed lines.
